title.narrative: DFAT Pacific Regional Aid for Trade Investment

description.narrative:
Funding under this investment is to support the sustainable trade development in the Pacific. In particular, it supports the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Secretariat's operations including funding the Pacific Aid for Trade Strategy, the Pacific Trade Invest (PTI) Australia and Europe, the PIF’s permanent representation to the WTO in Geneva. Given that Pacific Island countries rely on trade, tourism, and foreign direct investment, both offices’ work aligns well with Australia’s policy framework for support to the Pacific Islands in the post-COVID recovery era.
This funding enables the PIF's central role for advocating for Pacific interests in international forums, aligned with our region's commitment to rules-based trade.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia’s long-standing support for the Pacific Aid for Trade Strategy and e-commerce priorities assisted the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat to successfully launch its new E-Biz Plus program, supporting businesses utilise new digital approaches to expand their markets, including through tailored coaching and mentoring. It also provided grants to enhance their online presence, attract more customers, and boost sales. Hard Rock Sokehs in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) launched an e-commerce website, tripling its sales since September 2024. Talofa Studios in Tuvalu used the training and grants to improve product quality and internet connectivity, significantly boosting customer engagement. O-Tahiti Pearls in Samoa undertook a comprehensive marketing and branding upgrade, and as a result reported a 20% increase in online sales. Hilltop Hotel in FSM and Laban’s Gift Shop in Tuvalu secured listings on global and regional marketplaces, including Booking.com and Siuhuu, and are developing their own websites to further expand reach and customer base. The program also helped Tanny Island Sarong in Samoa, Hot Hula Fitness with Leony in Vanuatu, and Malekula Island Organic in Vanuatu develop e-commerce focussed business plans, increasing sales and brand visibility.

Australia’s longstanding support for the Pacific Islands Forum’s (PIF) permanent delegation to the World Trade Organization (WTO) continues to elevate the Pacific voice at the WTO and other multilateral organisations that are deeply rooted in the multilateral trading system. The PIF Secretariat’s Geneva office provided technical assistance to facilitate Pacific policy positions for negotiations on the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources, and Associated Traditional Knowledge (GRaTK). The GRaTK treaty, adopted in May 2024, was a significant step towards recognising and protecting traditional knowledge within the intellectual property framework, and to protecting genetic resources, and the interests of First Nations peoples and communities providing the traditional knowledge associated with them. This support helped underpin the Pacific’s growing influence on international trade-related issues, and demonstrated the important role played by the PIF Secretariat’s Geneva Office.

For over a decade PTI Australia has worked with the Samoa-based exporter to facilitate connections within the Australian market. With root crops being a competitive arena in Australia, PTI Australia focused on facilitating introductions to targeted importers and distributors and offering tangible business support such as the COVID-19 Freight Assistance Program and Packaging Support Program. ‍ Over the course of this work, PTI Australia supported the establishment and growth of the Samoa-based exporter in the Australian market. The outcome of this work included the facilitation of five deals between the Samoa-based exporter and key buyers within Australia.

In May 2024, the Geneva Office of the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat, funded by Australia, provided technical advice and coordinated positions for the 10 Pacific members of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) (Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Niue, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga and Vanuatu) who attended the WIPO diplomatic conference on intellectual property, genetic resources, and traditional knowledge (GRATK). The adoption of the new international treaty on GRATK ensures transparency through disclosure requirements. The Pacific members actively participated, collaborating with Australia and New Zealand to include a provision on technical cooperation and assistance informed by First Nations’ Australians perspectives. Three Pacific WIPO members signed the treaty at the diplomatic conference, and seven signed the final act, demonstrating strong regional commitment.
